logline: Based on real events in Uttar Pradesh, a no-nonsense IPS officer takes charge of a city split between two rival criminal empires and dismantles them through sheer force of will.

renewal.note: Two seasons aired on MX Player - Season 1 in May 2020 and Season 2 in January 2022. No further seasons have been announced.

seasons.review_body: Bhaukaal arrived on MX Player in May 2020 riding the wave of the UP-hinterland crime drama that Mirzapur had popularized. The show distinguishes itself by placing the camera squarely on the cop rather than the gangsters. Mohit Raina's SSP Navniet Sekera is the load-bearing performance: physically imposing, morally uncomplicated, and compelling enough to hold ten episodes of procedural confrontation. IWMBuzz described the show as 'a mofussil bloodbath' - a description that captures both its flaw and its appeal. Glamsham called it 'generic, but enjoyable nonetheless.' The IMDb audience score of 7.7 reflects solid engagement from audiences drawn to the UP-hinterland crime format, even when the writing did not rise above genre mechanics. English-language critical coverage was thin; the more enthusiastic response came from Hindi-press reviewers who appreciated the real-events grounding.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The IWMBuzz review called the premiere 'extremely predictable' in its opening moves but acknowledged Mohit Raina's performance as the no-nonsense SSP Naveen Sikhera carries the episode's weight. The setup - a new cop arrives in Muzaffarnagar to confront gangster Shaukeen and the Dedha Brothers - follows genre conventions closely, but the authentic Uttar Pradesh locations and Abhimanyu Singh's villain work provide enough texture to hold.
episode_reviews.the_moment: SSP Sikhera's first encounter with the criminal hierarchy of Muzaffarnagar - the show's thesis statement delivered through a single confrontational scene.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 4
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: IWMBuzz specifically singled out episode four for containing the season's best single set piece: a shootout staged in a sugarcane field that the review said 'deserves a shout-out'. The IWMBuzz verdict gave the series a mixed overall read but called this action sequence the show's most visually inventive moment - demonstrating that the production had ambitions beyond standard crime-drama staging.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The sugarcane field shootout - a chase and gunfight sequence staged with location-specific texture that IWMBuzz called the season's best action work.

critic_note.text: A shoot-out staged in a canefield that deserves a shout-out.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 returned in January 2022 with the Sekera-versus-Dedha conflict still centre-stage. BollywoodLife noted it 'starts slow and you start losing patience before it gets interesting' - a fair summary of the sophomore pattern where the show leans harder on action set-pieces than on the real-events texture that gave Season 1 its anchor. IANS gave three stars and described it as 'an inspiring film despite oodles of violence and tragedies.' Mohit Raina again carries the weight, and the actor's physical commitment to the role is not in dispute. The second season does not deepen the world so much as replay it with higher body counts. Viewers who enjoyed the first season's formula got exactly what they expected.
seasons.season_over_season: A slower start than Season 1 with diminishing novelty, though the Raina performance remains the constant.
